chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, and ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, all together from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurārah, who said:
I asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام about tayammum. He said: He struck the ground with his two hands, then raised them and shook them off, then wiped with them his forehead and his two palms once.

key_terms.التَّيَمُّمِ: dry ablution performed as a substitute for wudu (ablution) or ghusl (ritual bath) in specific circumstances
key_terms.الْأَرْضَ: the ground or earth used for tayammum
key_terms.فَنَفَضَهُمَا: then he shook them off lightly

ai.seo_question: How many times should the hands strike the earth in tayammum according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the method of tayammum as taught by Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام. It indicates that one striking of the earth followed by wiping the forehead and the palms is sufficient, making it an important proof in the jurisprudence of ritual purity.
